claims.claim_text_normalized: The Cascade R-CNN architecture consists of a sequence of detectors trained with increasing IoU thresholds.
claims.evidence_quote_short: It consists of a sequence of detectors trained with increasing IoU thresholds, to be sequentially more selective against close false positives.

claims.claim_text_normalized: Detection performance tends to degrade when the IoU threshold used for training is increased.
claims.evidence_quote_short: detection performance tends to degrade with increasing the IoU thresholds. Two main factors are responsible for this: 1) overfitting during training

claims.claim_text_normalized: The output of a detector trained with a given IoU threshold is a good distribution for training the next higher quality detector.
claims.evidence_quote_short: leveraging the observation that the output of a detector is a good distribution for training the next higher quality detector

claims.claim_text_normalized: A simple implementation of the Cascade R-CNN surpasses all single-model object detectors on the COCO dataset.
claims.evidence_quote_short: A simple implementation of the Cascade R-CNN is shown to surpass all single-model object detectors on the challenging COCO dataset

claims.claim_text_normalized: The Cascade R-CNN outperformed all single-model detectors by a large margin under all evaluation metrics.
claims.evidence_quote_short: The Cascade R-CNN also outperformed all single-model detectors by a large margin, under all evaluation metrics

claims.claim_text_normalized: Iterative bounding box regression usually provides no benefit beyond two applications.
claims.evidence_quote_short: Usually, there is no benefit beyond applying f twice.

claims.claim_text_normalized: The Cascade R-CNN improves baseline detectors consistently by roughly two to four AP points independently of baseline strength.
claims.evidence_quote_short: the Cascade R-CNN improves on these baselines consistently by 2~ 4 points, independently of their strength
